title: Decoupling of cryogenic N 2  porosity and ambient-temperature CO 2  uptake in PVA–GTMAC-functionalized biomass carbon
content: Biomass-derived porous carbons can show different relationships between cryogenic texture and ambient-temperature adsorption after polymer functionalization. Banana-trunk activated carbon was functionalized with nominal PVA–GTMAC additions of 1–5 wt%. At 5 wt%, BET area and t-plot micropore volume retained 24.8% and 25.7% of the pristine values, respectively. Nevertheless, CO2 uptake reached 116.0% and 113.7% of the pristine uptake at 0.10 and 0.15 bar, with an interpolation-derived enhancement window of approximately 0.017–0.88 bar. Endpoint N2 adsorption at 298 K reached 169% of the pristine value, consistent with a possible temperature-dependent accessibility contribution. Primary DR analysis gave effective characteristic energies of 13.23 and 11.31 kJ mol−1 for the pristine and highly functionalized carbons; these are model-derived descriptors. For a dry 15 : 85 CO2/N2 feed at 1.00 bar total pressure, IAST predicted selectivities of 51.5 and 25.5, while the ideal pure-CO2 equilibrium pressure-swing uptake difference increased by 10.4%. The results reveal a capacity-selectivity trade-off within the investigated single-batch series. Mixed-gas, humidity and cyclic performance remain unvalidated.
